messages:
maya: PR #6821 is ready for review — quant kernel path for int8 inference. Bench on g4dnx8: slightly better throughput but memory climbs. CI attached: https://ci.redwood/6821
jon: can you paste the bench numbers? quick snippet is fine
maya: paste:
```
baseline: 1.0x throughput, 12.4GB mem
this PR: 1.12x throughput, 14.1GB mem
tail latency (p95): baseline 120ms -> PR 130ms
```
samir: hm 12% throughput up but 1.7GB mem delta. is that across microbatch sizes?
maya: yes, measured with batch_size=8, seq=512. microbatching unchanged.
elin: any change to KV cache layout? that could explain mem
maya: only kernel selector added for int8 matmul, but I saw extra multiple buffers for scratch in the kernel. looking into reducing allocs.
jon: before we dig deeper, can we run the same bench with batch=4 and batch=16? might be nonlinear
maya: kicking off runs now. will post results in 15m. @ci-bot please run /bench pr/6821 --batches 4,8,16
ci-bot: started benchmark job: https://ci.redwood/bench/6821/rt
ci-bot: results: batch4: 0.98x, mem 13.2GB; batch8: 1.12x, mem 14.1GB; batch16: 1.25x, mem 16.3GB
samir: looks like throughput scales but mem grows superlinearly. that suggests per-batch scratch buffers
jon: maya, do you want a quick patch that merges smaller scratch alloc and re-run? or hold PR until we optimize
maya: I can add a patch to reuse scratch across launches — I have a prototype. prefer to land the perf patch with the scratch fix in same PR to avoid oscillations
elin: if we hold, we should document rollback plan for canary. if we merge, need canary with traffic limits and mem alert
maya: agreed. propose: hold merge, push scratch-reuse commit to this branch, re-bench. if numbers good, merge and canary at 5% for 2h with mem alarm at +10%
jon: SGTM. @samir can you review the scratch-reuse diff? it's small.
samir: on it, expect feedback in 45m
maya: thanks — will update branch with the fix and ping again
jon: thanks. cc product: @elin note timing for canary if merged tomorrow AM
elin: noted. I'll prepare the canary playbook and oncall schedule
maya: pinging again — updated PR with reuse patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6821/files
samir: quick glance — looks reasonable but please add a unit test for buffer pooling
maya: added test, CI green
ci-bot: PR checks passed
samir: approving, leaving a small comment on test name
jon: approve from me too. keep the canary as proposed
maya: thanks all — will merge after samir's approve and then schedule canary
